subject: History
description: Roy, Vidyasagar, Phule, Naoroji, Gokhale, Tilak — reforms, movements, dates

questions.stem: The FOUNDER of Brahmo Samaj (1828) was:
questions.explanation: Raja Ram Mohan Roy — 'Father of modern India' / 'Father of Indian Renaissance'. Founded Brahmo Samaj in Calcutta, 1828. Campaigned against sati (abolished by Regulation XVII of 1829 under Bentinck); pioneered women's education. Dayananda founded Arya Samaj (1875).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's landmark contribution was:
questions.explanation: Vidyasagar's tireless campaigning led Lord Dalhousie to the Hindu Widows' Remarriage Act, 1856. Also promoted women's education (founded Hindu Female Schools), simplified Bangla primers (Borno Porichoy). Sati abolition (1829) was Ram Mohan Roy's victory under Bentinck.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Match the REFORMER with their ORGANISATION / WORK. A. Jyotirao Phule.  B. Dayananda Saraswati.  C. Swami Vivekananda.  D. Annie Besant. List-II: 1. Satyashodhak Samaj (1873).  2. Arya Samaj (1875).  3. Ramakrishna Mission (1897).  4. Theosophical Society (India, 1893).
questions.explanation: Phule — Satyashodhak Samaj ('Truth-Seekers' Society'), Pune 1873 — anti-caste, women's education. Dayananda — Arya Samaj (Bombay 1875), 'Back to the Vedas'. Vivekananda — founded RKM 1897 (philanthropic arm of Ramakrishna order). Besant — led the Theosophical Society in India from 1893 (HQ Adyar).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: 'DRAIN THEORY' — critiquing the systematic transfer of wealth from India to Britain — was propounded by:
questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji articulated the 'Drain Theory' — most famously in 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901). Estimated the annual drain at £30-40 million. R. C. Dutt further elaborated it. Tilak was the 'Lokmanya' extremist; Gokhale was Gandhi's 'political guru'.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Who among the following gave the slogan 'SWARAJ IS MY BIRTHRIGHT, and I SHALL have it'?
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak ('Lokmanya') popularised this slogan, during his Home Rule agitation in 1917. Founded Ganapati (1893) and Shivaji Jayanti (1895) festivals as political mobilisation tools. Newspapers: Kesari (Marathi), Mahratta (English).
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Raja Ram Mohan Roy's most important journalistic contribution was:
questions.explanation: Sambad Kaumudi (1821 weekly Bengali) and Mirat-ul-Akhbar (1822 Persian) — pioneering vernacular journalism. Amrita Bazar Patrika (1868) was founded by Sisir Kumar Ghosh. Bombay Samachar (1822) is India's oldest continuously-published newspaper.
questions.subject: History

questions.stem: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded which organisation, and is remembered as the 'political guru' of:

options.option_text: Servants of India Society, 1905 — political guru of Mahatma Gandhi
Home Rule League — guru of Patel

questions.explanation: Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in 1905 (Pune) to train 'national missionaries'. Gandhi addressed Gokhale as his political guru; Gokhale toured South Africa in 1912 at Gandhi's invitation. Moderate Congress phase 1905-1915. Died 1915.
